issues.title: Named Ops complaint investigator can read detail but cannot list their own assignments
Another complaint desk cannot look up a tracking number to take its appeal
Complaint acknowledgement's named people directory omits permitted staff investigators
Withdrawn unacknowledged complaint returns acknowledgement with None and blank deadline
Screening excludes draft unexpected deaths; certification prerequisite is undocumented
Action register bundle omits department directory for its documented department filter
ADR report bundle omits the ADR incident selector source
Transfusion registers bundle omits the stock source for unit trace
Blood center return bundle omits the period donation directory

endpoints.description:
Newest first (the period by the day received). Without `complaint.view` or `complaint.manage`, whatever the
caller's role, `mine` is implied: the complaints they received, investigate or took the appeal of. So the member of
staff named investigator lists theirs on "Complaints I investigate" (`?mine=true&status=Acknowledged`) without any
complaint permission, and a caller with none of these gets an empty list. `acknowledgement_overdue` and
`answer_overdue` in red. A complaint another desk received is found by its tracking number
(`GET /complaints/by-number/{complaint_number}`), never by browsing.

access.who: any logged-in user: the whole register with complaint.view or complaint.manage; anyone else the complaints they received, investigate or took the appeal of (mine is implied)

endpoints.description:
For the complaint readers, the person who received it, its investigator and the desk that took its appeal: with
every contact with the complainant (`updates`), the actions, `next_step` and what the caller may do (`can_*`).
`FORBIDDEN` for anyone else: another desk reads the complaint's card by its tracking number
(`GET /complaints/by-number/{complaint_number}`). Reading one about a patient is logged as a patient-data access.

access.who: complaint.view or complaint.manage, the person who received the complaint, its investigator and the person who took its appeal

endpoints.description:
A complainant brings their tracking number to any desk, to ask how it stands or to appeal the outcome
(decision 63, backend issue #57): the card says how it stands, never what the complaint says, the patient, the
findings or the outcome. Confirm `complainant_name` with the person at the desk first. Then, while `can_appeal`,
take the appeal (`POST /complaints/{complaint_id}/appeal`): from then on that desk opens the complaint like the desk
that received it (`can_open`). Exact numbers only: there is no search, so a desk never browses the register.
`NOT_FOUND`: no complaint has that number.

**Required permission:** `complaint.register OR complaint.view OR complaint.manage`

**Required permission:** `complaint.register OR complaint.view OR complaint.manage`

access.who: holders of complaint.register or complaint.view or complaint.manage

endpoints.description:
At any complaint desk, within the window the outcome gave (`COMPLAINT_APPEAL_LATE` after it). A desk that did not
receive the complaint finds it by the tracking number first (`GET /complaints/by-number/{complaint_number}`,
`can_appeal`); the answer is the whole complaint, which that desk reads from then on (decision 63). The appeal
deciders are notified.

`COMPLAINT_STATE_INVALID`: only a Resolved complaint is appealed.

**Required permission:** `complaint.register OR complaint.manage`

**Required permission:** `complaint.register OR complaint.manage`

Within `complaint_acknowledge_hours` (MSDS PRE 82 ii a): the priority, the contact person, the investigator
(default: the contact person; both any active member of staff with a login, whatever their role, from
`GET /quality/record-review/people`: backend issue #58), the course of action and the date the outcome is due (default
`complaint_response_days` after receipt); `means` says how the complainant was told (recorded as an update). Or
`maintainable` false with the reason. Then print the letter (`GET /complaints/{id}/letter/print-payload`).
`COMPLAINT_STATE_INVALID`: the complaint cannot change that way: what was complained of, the acknowledgement, the
outcome and the appeal are recorded once.

**Required permission:** `complaint.manage`

**Required permission:** `complaint.manage`

The same letters as the print payload, when it has them. `COMPLAINT_STATE_INVALID`: the complaint has not reached
this letter's step (the acknowledgement before it is acknowledged, or of a complaint withdrawn before that).

access.who: complaint.view or complaint.manage, the person who received the complaint, its investigator and the person who took its appeal

endpoints.description:
The acknowledgement, the outcome with the right to appeal, or the appeal decision, in English with the Urdu
sentences in `fields.urdu` (render right to left on the terminal). Each letter exists once its step happened,
whatever the status became later: `Acknowledgement` once `acknowledged_at` is set (acknowledged, or answered not
maintainable), `Outcome` once `outcome_at`, `AppealOutcome` once `appeal_decided_at`. A complaint withdrawn after
its acknowledgement reprints that letter as sent; one withdrawn before it has no letter.
`COMPLAINT_STATE_INVALID`: the complaint has not reached that letter's step (backend issue #59).

access.who: complaint.view or complaint.manage, the person who received the complaint, its investigator and the person who took its appeal

endpoints.description:
Every active member of staff with a login, by name: the picker of every form that may name anyone, whatever
their role (an action's owner, an incident's investigator, a complaint's contact person and investigator, a
committee's members), and of the record review panel (only those with `can_review`: the panel refuses the
others). The facts of their badge only, as `GET /staff/lookup` gives them to anyone
(its search suits a large hospital better), so every user may call it: the investigator named on an incident picks
the owner of an action from it on the shared screen "Incidents I investigate" (backend issue #58, after #41).

Returns to theatre and readmissions within 24 hours, unexpected, maternal and post-operative deaths and suicides
of the last `incident_screening_days`, not yet reported or dismissed (MSDS CQI 106): report each (`POST /incidents`
with `screening_key` and the suggested type) or dismiss it with the reason.

Each kind appears once the records it reads are final (backend issue #60):
* ReturnToTheatre: an operation that started within `incident_screening_hours` of the end of the patient's previous
  operation (both with their actual times; a cancelled one never counts);
* Readmission: an admission within `incident_screening_hours` of the patient's previous discharge;
* Death: once the death is **certified** (`POST /deaths/{death_id}/certify`; a draft's facts may still change),
  never one brought dead: recorded by the doctor as unexpected (`expected_death` false), a suicide (manner
  IntentionalSelfHarm), a maternal death (pregnancy at death or within 42 days), or within four weeks of an
  operation.
Already reported as an incident for the same operation, admission or death, or dismissed: not listed.

**Required permission:** `incident.view`

**Required permission:** `incident.view`

The departments by name: the directory every form that names a department picks from (`department_id`,
`target_department_id`), so nobody types an id: the incident and complaint forms, the corrective actions of every
register, the duty rosters, the equipment and asset registers, the compliance register, the mock drills, the waste
log, the training sessions, the job descriptions, the service catalogue and HR's onboarding (decision 62). Offer the
active ones (`is_active`); clinical departments carry `is_clinical`. The IT console adds and edits them
(`POST /admin/departments`, `PUT /admin/departments/{department_id}`).
